newsitem.title: UK: British Air facing strike threat over catering sale.
newsitem.headline: British Air facing strike threat over catering sale.

text.p: British Airways Plc was threatened with a strike by ground staff at its London Heathrow and Gatwick airports Monday over plans to sell its Heathrow catering production division.
The Transport and General Work Union said a job action would involve its 9,000 ground staff members, including baggage handlers, clerical and check-in workers as well as the catering staff.
The union said the result of a strike vote will be announced June 30, just as the summer travel season gets into full swing.
The airline vowed to keep services going if there is a strike.

"The T&G announcement represents only an intention to ballot. There is no commitment from staff to strike and we hope that staff will reject this suggestion because there is absolutely no justification for it," said a company spokesman. "We have contingency plans in place and come what may we will continue to fly," he said.
BA put the long-haul catering business up for sale in April as part of its "business efficiency" campaign, aimed at finding $1.5 billion in savings in annual costs from outsourcing and cutbacks.

The union accused BA management of wanting to create a "virtual airline" selling little more than a brand of service operated by outside contractors, something British Airways Chief Executive Robert Ayling has denied.
